issues.area: flaky requirement test on the iOS Simulator (R-SYN-12)
issues.location: Tests/ZTronAssetSyncTests/Engine/EngineEventsTests.swift:87-112 (`R-SYN-12: transfer progress published to subscribers never exceeds 10 Hz per asset under ManualTimeSource`)
issues.problem: The test failed in simulator run 1 and passed in simulator run 2. xcresult for run 1: 997 tests, 996 passed, 1 failed, failure 'Expectation failed: progress.count >= 2 / progress.count → 1: progress flows'. The lower bound counts events that the collector Task has actually consumed. Under backpressure (ARCHITECTURE §7.9), progress coalesces newest-wins in one slot per key, and that key retires with the transfer. So a collector that is not scheduled during the 50 rounds sees at most one event. The engine is behaving correctly here; the oracle depends on scheduling. I proved the mechanism in a scratch copy: a variant whose collector starts pulling only after the rounds (a starved pool) failed 2 of 2 runs at the same expectation. On macOS the test passed 3 of 3 runs and under TSan.
issues.fix: Make the lower bound deterministic. After each round's release and clock advance, wait until the stream has drained, for example `await engine.awaitCondition { $0.state.subscribers.values.allSatisfy { $0.liveCount == 0 } }`, so the collector consumes each emission before the next one is offered. Alternatively, assert the lower bound on the engine's offered or published progress count rather than on consumed events. Keep the `<= ceiling` bound. Then rerun the simulator command.

issues.area: time budget under TSan: a test timed out (flake)
issues.location: Tests/ZTronAssetSyncTests/Engine/EngineRunPathTests.swift:361 (`R-SYN-6: a pending run whose gate opens while the blocked run is still finishing starts once it has finished`, .timeLimit(.minutes(1)), 500 iterations)
issues.problem: TSan full-suite run 2 failed: 'Time limit was exceeded: 60.000 seconds' at :361, then 'Expectation failed: resumed != nil' at :396 because the test was cancelled. The test failed after 64.984 s. The load average rose from 6.65 to 73.85 during that run, because other agents were working. TSan run 1 passed, but the test took 55.882 s, 93 % of its limit, at a load average of about 15-25. Run alone under TSan it takes 3.939 s, and in debug 2.2-13.7 s. The cost comes from contention with the other 202 parallel tests under the sanitizer, which the 1-minute limit does not absorb. TSan reported 0 races in either run.
issues.fix: Lower the test's cost under contention. For example, force each of the two orders deterministically with a NextUnitGate or SteppedBlockingExecutor instead of relying on 500 racing iterations. Or reduce the iteration count and yield once per iteration (ios.md item 8). Otherwise give it a limit with real headroom (e.g. .timeLimit(.minutes(3))) and record the in-suite TSan figures in F-17.

issues.area: correctness / data loss: an interest that follows new content the apply already made present downloads it again, and a 404 on that download marks the present asset failed (T22, §7.1 'only outstanding work has a job', R-NET-6/ADR-032)
issues.location: Sources/ZTronAssetSync/Engine/EngineRuns.swift:331-385 (applied/followApplied ignore report.reused and report.relocated); Sources/ZTronAssetSync/Engine/EngineDispatch.swift:777-815 (reroute calls addInterest at :814 for an entry the store already holds); Sources/ZTronAssetSync/Engine/EngineFailures.swift:110-123 (permanentMissing calls store.recordFailure(job.assets, …) at :117)
issues.problem: Timeline: a waiter for x@c1 is downloading. A run applies v2, where x's new content equals y's content, which is already present. The store reuses y's blob, so x is present and verified right after the apply (probe printed 'x residency after apply=present(…verified)', plan reuseCount 1). followApplied supersedes x@c1, and reroute calls addInterest on y's transfer. That creates a new job and downloads content the store already holds. PROBE-R3-3 (3 of 3 runs): the waiter succeeded only after 'y-content starts=2' (expected 1). PROBE-R3-3b (3 of 3 runs) is the same, except that redundant fetch answers 404. The engine calls recordFailure([x], identity) on a record that is present. The probe saw 'waiter=failure(notFound) x=failed(notFound) y=present', and a fresh resolve(x) afterwards returned 'failure(notFound)'. A valid local copy is unbound and the asset is unavailable until its entry changes. A CDN that publishes the manifest before the object makes this 404 realistic. The same path applies to prefetch, run and ensure interests rerouted by any apply, including an ensureAvailable apply during a run.
issues.fix: In applied(), collect report.reused ∪ report.relocated (the ids the apply made present). In followApplied and reroute, do not call addInterest for those ids; answer them from the store in an owned task (store.location: a waiter gets the location, a group drops the member as done, a run counts the asset as fetched). More generally, never create a job for an id whose record is present at its current identity. As a safety net, call recordFailure only for ids the engine knows are absent, and ask the orchestrator whether WP-C's recordFailure should skip present records. Add PROBE-R3-3 and PROBE-R3-3b as regression tests.

issues.area: round-2 regression: ensureAvailable re-downloads members committed by another interest after its plan (S1-15 materialisation)
issues.location: Sources/ZTronAssetSync/Engine/EngineDispatch.swift:112-142 (materializeEnsures turns each fetch into a job from state.applied without a presence check); Sources/ZTronAssetSync/Engine/EngineCommands.swift:371-375 (group.fetches = plan.fetches); same window in EngineRuns.swift:429 materializeRun (F-19) and in joinGroup (RE-S30)
issues.problem: Round 2 made ensureAvailable materialise its fetches a pipeline at a time. Before that, all fetches registered in one turn and joined existing jobs. Now an asset that another interest commits between the ensure's plan and its materialisation is downloaded again. PROBE-R3-2 (tuning: 1 slot, pipelineDepth 1, lookahead 0; 3 of 3 runs): ensureAvailable([e0, e1]) holds e0 (failed once, waiting for its retry). A prefetch then downloads and commits e1 (probe saw 'e1 residency after the prefetch: present(…verified)'). After e0's retry, the ensure materialises e1 and downloads it again: 'e1 starts=2' (expected 1). The window now spans the whole ensureAvailable call, not just one await. By the same recordFailure path as PROBE-R3-3b (proven there), a 404 on such a redundant fetch marks the present asset failed.
issues.fix: Keep a set of ids bound since the plan. committed() fills it from the keys of `locations`, and applied() from report.reused/relocated, for each ensure group (and for the run). materializeEnsures and materializeRun skip fetches in that set and count them as done. This also closes F-19 for runs. Add PROBE-R3-2 as a regression test.

issues.area: space policy (R-SYN-11, S2-23): ensureAvailable writes a doctored free-space reading into the shared headroom ledger, and round 2's re-evaluation then starts opportunistic work
issues.location: Sources/ZTronAssetSync/Engine/EngineCommands.swift:313-335 (space built with volumeOpportunistic: measured.volumeImportant at :319; self.state.freeSpace = space at :333; reconsiderSpaceBlocked() at :335, new in round 2)
issues.problem: ensureTask plans user work against important capacity, which is correct for its own plan. But it stores that copy, with opportunistic capacity overwritten by the important figure, as the engine-wide ledger base. Every prefetch or bulk job checked against the ledger until the next real read is therefore admitted against important capacity. Round 2's reconsiderSpaceBlocked() goes further and re-queues the parked ones at once. PROBE-R3-1 (3 of 3 runs): FakeFileSystem has importantCapacity 64 GiB and opportunisticCapacity = reserve + 100 bytes. The store reports 'important=68719476104 opportunistic=268434924 reserve=268435456'. A 300-byte prefetch is parked (blocked). After ensureAvailable(scope: [q]) the probe saw 'p state=downloading starts=1', where the prefetch should stay parked because opportunistic capacity did not change.
issues.fix: Keep `measured` as self.state.freeSpace (and reconsider against it). Pass the important-for-opportunistic copy only to the planner and to the ensure's own space decision. Add PROBE-R3-1 as a regression test.

issues.area: staging hygiene (R-CLN-3; extends round-2 PROBE-R2-F): the partial of an attempt that failed with ENOSPC is never discarded
issues.location: Sources/ZTronAssetSync/Engine/EngineFailures.swift:140-144 (the .insufficientSpace case goes to spaceFailed without resumePoint or discard) and :281-306 (spaceFailed)
issues.problem: The store's staging sink leaves the bytes written before ENOSPC in the attempt's .part (StoreStagingSink.appendPartial does not remove it), and the transport reports .insufficientSpace without discarding it. The engine's ENOSPC path never calls resumePoint(after:) or staging.discard, unlike the transient and pause paths fixed in round 2. The dead partial occupies exactly the space that is short, until a launch or maintenance GC. PROBE-R3-4 (3 of 3 runs): 120 bytes are written into attempt 1's partial and the attempt fails with insufficientSpace(300) on a roomy volume. The retry succeeds and the job ends, but stagingInventory still holds 'c-2ac19…​.1-2.part'.
issues.fix: In the .insufficientSpace case, discard request.partialName (and any sidecar) before the free-space read. Alternatively, route it through resumePoint(after:) so a sidecar-backed partial is kept for resume and any other partial is discarded. Add PROBE-R3-4 as a regression test.

issues.area: round-2 probes C and G no longer fit the design (fixes confirmed with adapted probes)
issues.location: Tests/ZTronAssetSyncTests/Engine/EngineRegressionRound2Tests.swift (WP versions); scratch probes ZZVerifierR2ProbeTests C and G
issues.problem: Run unchanged against HEAD, PROBE-R2-C times out in waitUntil(blocked == 1), because a transient ENOSPC on a roomy volume is now retried rather than parked. PROBE-R2-G times out because the fix makes the late joiner's content download a second time and the probe scripted one attempt. The adapted PROBE-R3-C2 (waits for failed, advances the clock) and PROBE-R3-G2 (scripts a second stage) both pass, so both blocking items are fixed. G's second download in this race is the tradeoff F-20 documents. Avoiding it needs a store call that binds an id to a live blob, which is a contract change.

issues.area: headroom ledger: commits between a free-space read and its adoption are lost (S2-09), by reading
issues.problem: Both the run and ensureAvailable await store.freeSpace(), then await planningView(), and only then set state.freeSpace and committedSinceRead = 0. A publication that commits between the read and the reset adds to committedSinceRead, and the reset drops it. The ledger then overstates headroom by those bytes until the next read. Not proven with a probe.
issues.fix: Adopt the read in the turn it returns, before planningView. Alternatively, stamp commits with a sequence and subtract only those after the read.

issues.area: catch-up path skips applied()'s bookkeeping, by reading
issues.location: Sources/ZTronAssetSync/Engine/EngineCatchUp.swift:51-63 (catchUpWithStore: adoptApplied with the old ETag, then followApplied)
issues.problem: When the store's manifest differs from the engine's copy and no apply is in flight, the engine adopts it but broadcasts no assetRemoved(.pruned) and no snapshotChanged, and leaves the generation and the old ETag unchanged. In production this happens when store.apply throws after its in-memory writes (AssetStore+Apply.swift:67 requireCommittedInternal). A later re-apply of the same manifest reports pruned = [], so those removal events are lost for good. Not proven with a probe.
issues.fix: On catch-up, broadcast assetRemoved(.pruned) for ids in the copy but missing from the view, take the view's generation, then send snapshotChanged. Alternatively, in applyAndFollow, re-read the store view after a failed apply and follow it.

open: Needs a ruling (F-15): a run whose manifest fetch passed manifestFetchDeadline now ends .complete with manifestFresh == false but writes no stamp, so the sync stays due. The alternative is .completeWithFailures. ARCHITECTURE §7.10's rule 'markSynced only for .complete' would then read 'only for a .complete run with a fresh manifest'.

Decision to confirm (F-16): an offline run is retried once after the debounce. A second offline run in a row, while the path reads satisfied, then waits for a satisfied-path edge. Waiting for an edge after every offline run (the verifier's first option) broke 'R-SYN-6: a pending run whose gate opens while the blocked run is still finishing starts once it has finished', whose single offline failure must still be retried.

New, not fixed (found this round, efficiency only): a run's plan is a snapshot. If another interest commits a planned asset after the run's planning view but before the run creates the job, the run downloads it again; the store deduplicates the blob. A rerouted interest whose new content is already present also starts a redundant job. In 'R-CAR-2: an identifier a run's fetched manifest lists is never answered notFound before the run applies it' the redundant attempt hung the run about 1 in 20 suite runs until I scripted a second attempt.
